title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Sofia Martinez
description: Motivation: reduce unit token cost for common workloads by providing safe, production-ready defaults and automation for batching/caching and quantization profile selection, and ship unit-economics tooling so customers can quickly reason about cost/latency trade-offs. This PR introduces: 1) autotune defaults service that recommends batching (max_batch_size, latency SLO windows) and prefix/KV caching defaults per model/profile; 2) a set of vetted quantization profiles (int8/qat/pgd variants) with compatibility constraints and fallbacks; 3) a small Redwood Console integration + CLI (redwood optimize uecon) to simulate unit economics across workload traces; 4) a public API endpoint for Unit Econ estimates used by the Console and by internal autopilot to pick defaults. See ENG-1249 for full scope. Checklist: - [x] implement autotune defaults service and persisted profiles - [x] add quantization profile registry + compatibility matrix - [x] expose unit-econ endpoint and CLI simulator - [x] integrate defaults into serving runtime routing decisions - [x] add E2E tests and performance benchmarks - [x] update docs and console UI wire-up - [x] run canary on dedicated fleet and monitor regressions Rollout plan: feature gated behind feature.autotune_defaults; enabled for internal canary teams for 2 weeks, then gradual 10/25/50/100% rollout. Backout: revert feature flag and fallback to conservative defaults. Impact: expected 8-15% token-cost reduction on mixed production traffic in our beta customers; no user-visible quality changes because fallback quant profiles are more conservative and we keep canary comparisons. Related: ENG-1311 (quant profiles), PM-442 (console UEcon UX), SUP-978 (customer request for cost tooling).
